adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: H pylori urease hydrolyzes urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide. Ammonia buffers protons and creates a locally less acidic microenvironment that supports gastric colonization.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Urease production is also exploited diagnostically by the urea breath test, but the question asks its survival function. Ammonia-mediated local buffering is the direct acid-resistance mechanism.
